August 9, 1965. A man sits before a television camera and weeps. His country has just been expelled, left to rot on a swampy island with no water, no resources, and no hope.

Fifty years later, that same island is the richest patch of land on the planet.

This is the true story of Lee Kuan Yew and the rise of Singapore. From a "poisonous shrimp" defense strategy to a ruthless obsession with efficiency, Singapore wasn't just a nation... it was a corporate startup disguised as a country. Fueled by "Asian values," zero-tolerance laws, and a total refusal to fail.
